can_you_chat_with_jev.instructions: Can you chat with Jev, TypeSafe's new model?

understands_natural_language.instructions: Does Jev understand natural language input?

output_type.instructions: What kind of output does Jev produce?

similarity_to_wrappers.instructions: How similar is Jev's architecture to an LLM wrapper prompted to output JSON?
criteria: Nothing in common, in concept or in execution
Slight conceptual overlap, but fundamentally different inner workings
Substantial overlap in both concept and execution with similar inner workings
Nearly the same, differing only in the surface-level details

confidence_mechanism.instructions: How does Jev arrive at the confidence behind an answer?

who_shapes_the_answer.instructions: Who defines the shape of Jev's answer space?
criteria: The person asking — each question defines the structure of its own answer
Both — the asker and Jev share it
Jev alone — he picks his own format

capital_of_america.instructions: Can Jev answer "What's the capital of America?" as a normal chat question?

noul_has_separate_confidence.instructions: Does a Noul answer include a separate confidence field in addition to the yes/no probability?

questions_evaluated_in_parallel.instructions: Are multiple questions in a single Jev request evaluated independently and in parallel against the same state?

can_invent_outside_criteria.instructions: Can a successful Jev answer return a value outside the options or levels the asker defined?

what_score_number_means.instructions: What does the numeric value of a Score answer represent?

criteria.The probability-weighted mean of the ord: A distribution of 70% on level 1 and 30% on level 2 returns 1.3
criteria.A free-form rating the model invents out: The model writes its own number

primitive_for_yes_no_gate.instructions: Which primitive should you use when your code gates a single yes/no branch?

criteria.Choice with two named options plus a con: Heavier shape for the same yes/no information
criteria.Score over unordered categories: A weighted mean of things with no order
criteria.Noul, a probability from 0 to 1 that the: One number; near 0.5 is maximum uncertainty

what_confidence_summarizes.instructions: For Choice and Score, what does the confidence value summarize?

criteria.How peaked the probability distribution: Mass on one option is high; mass spread across several is low
criteria.The winning option's raw probability, an: Ignores a close runner-up versus a scattered tail
criteria.A prose explanation of how sure the mode: The model is asked to say how confident it is

choice_for_ordered_scale.instructions: How appropriate is a Choice with options like "low", "medium", and "high" when what you need is a position on an ordered scale?
criteria: The right primitive — Choice preserves order and in-between values
The wrong primitive — you lose the ordering and the in-between Score value

atomic_question_design.instructions: How strongly should a complex Jev judgment be split into narrow, explicit, atomic questions in one request?
criteria: Always prefer one broad question that does the whole analysis
Split only when latency would otherwise explode
Ask the most explicit, narrow, atomic questions you can; they run in parallel so four narrow ones beat one broad one

noul_half_is_uncertainty.instructions: How close is a Noul value of 0.5 to maximum uncertainty?
criteria: It is maximum uncertainty — yes and no are equally likely, and there is no separate confidence field
It is a medium yes, like a mid-scale Score
